title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 101: The Antikythera Mechanism
passageHtml:
READING A2 (BAND 4.0) — BÀI 101

The Antikythera Mechanism

Paragraph 1. In the spring of 1900, a group of Greek divers sailed home from North Africa. Suddenly, a big storm hit their boat. They stopped near a small island called Antikythera. When the weather became calm, one diver named Elias Stadiatis went under the sea to look for sea sponges (soft sea animals). He went down 45 metres in a heavy metal helmet. When he came back up, he looked very scared. He told his friends about old statues and bronze horses on the sea floor. He had found an ancient Roman ship that sank long ago.

Paragraph 2. Later that year, Greek workers spent nine months bringing the old objects out of the water. They took the treasures to a museum in Athens. One object looked like a dirty, broken rock of green metal. For nearly two years, nobody paid attention to it, and it stayed outside in a yard. Then, in May 1902, a scientist named Valerios Stais looked at the rock carefully. The rock had broken open. Inside, Stais saw a small metal wheel with sharp teeth. Many experts did not believe it was ancient. They thought someone from a newer ship dropped a clock into the sea.

Paragraph 3. In the 1950s, a British scientist named Derek de Solla Price studied the object with X-ray machines. His pictures showed that the pieces came from one small machine, about the size of a house clock. Long ago, it sat inside a wooden box. On the outside, bronze plates gave instructions on how to use it. The machine was about 2,100 years old and had at least thirty metal wheels inside. A person turned a handle on the side to move all the wheels together.

Paragraph 4. This ancient machine was like an early computer for the sky. The front part had circles that showed the days of the year and the positions of the sun and the moon. On the back, other dials could tell people the exact time of future moon eclipses (when the moon goes dark). In 2005, scientists used special 3D cameras to look deep inside the broken pieces. They discovered tiny Greek letters and learned that the machine also followed the paths of five planets. It proved that ancient Greek engineers were much smarter than people had thought.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage?
Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "a big storm hit their boat. They stopped near a small island called Antikythera." (big = strong).
Đoạn 2: "For nearly two years, nobody paid attention to it, and it stayed outside in a yard."
Đoạn 3: "Long ago, it sat inside a wooden box." (wooden = made of wood).
Đoạn 4: "...learned that the machine also followed the paths of five planets." (followed = tracked).

q5.text: Elias Stadiatis went into the sea to look for old statues.

steps: Đoạn 1: Anh ta lặn xuống để tìm bọt biển (went under the sea to look for sea sponges), không phải tìm tượng cổ.

q6.text: At first, many experts thought the metal wheel was not very old.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Many experts did not believe it was ancient." (did not believe it was ancient = thought it was not very old).

q7.text: Derek de Solla Price built a working copy of the ancient machine.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài chỉ nói ông dùng máy X-ray để nghiên cứu cổ vật (studied the object with X-ray machines), không nhắc ông có tự làm ra bản sao chạy được hay không.

q8.text: The 2005 study showed that ancient Greek engineers had more skill than people previously believed.

steps: Đoạn 4: "It proved that ancient Greek engineers were much smarter than people had thought."
